goal: Let quality, finances and agent-ledger enforce the change record check (H16 step 3) without failing the weekly brief and import pull requests, which change data a person reviews, not code. Also fix the no-comments record's claim 4, which cited a commit GitHub didn't have (H16 step 4).
changed: debrief.py check --base reads a repo's own exempt paths from .changes/exempt on the base branch: one literal path per line, a directory covering everything under it, # for comments. A pull request that adds or widens the list is still held to the old one, and one that leaves a bad line in it fails. A bad list on the base is ignored with a warning, so every path then needs a record.

The BOOKKEEPING tuple shared with receipt.py and check-product.py is unchanged, because those use it to decide when a verify-work receipt goes stale, and books/ and ledger/ are data those checks must see.

Claim 4 of .changes/2026-11-21-no-comments.json still cites 58bc6e8, the text the trial ran on. The tag trial/2026-11-21-no-comments keeps that commit on GitHub, and the claim now says which two changes in main's e548abb were never tried.

claims.claim: The check honours a base-branch .changes/exempt, holds a pull request to the base's list rather than its own, matches each entry literally from the root, still asks for a record when code changes beside exempt data, fails a pull request that leaves a bad list, and ignores a bad list on the base.
claims.check: tests/test_debrief.py, 41 tests (7 new) on throwaway git repos with python3 3.9; make check validate unit (1278 tests, Python 3.12). Three mutations each fail a new test: the old debrief.py (7 fail), plain :(exclude) instead of :(exclude,literal) (the literal-match test fails), reading the list from HEAD instead of the base (the self-exemption test fails).
claims.remaining: Nothing checks that an entry names data rather than code; that is left to review of the PR that edits the list.

claims.claim: With the planned lists, the enforced check passes every brief and import pull request (quality #26 and #38, finances #25, #27, #29 and #30, agent-ledger #32 and #33) and still fails the code and workflow pull requests that carried no record.
claims.check: replay.sh: each PR since 2026-11-21 in the three repos, plus finances #16, #21 and #22 as controls, merged into its base plus the planned .changes/exempt and checked with this branch's debrief.py, no --observe. Verdicts were written from each PR's changed files before the run, and all matched. Failing as expected: quality #22, #23, #25, #40, #44; finances #16, #21, #22; agent-ledger #28, #35, #36.
claims.remaining: Four records already merged under observe are invalid (VERIFIED with no commit): quality and finances .changes/2026-11-22-local-ci.json and 2026-11-22-drop-ledger-bootstrap.json. They fail the replay of #39, #41, #31 and #32, and will fail any later pull request that edits them. quality's briefs/ entry also exempts briefs/TEMPLATE.md, which shapes the weekly job's output.

claims.claim: Claim 4 of the no-comments record now passes on a clone of GitHub, and only because of the tag.
claims.check: Fresh clones of this branch from GitHub: with tags, debrief.py check --base origin/main reports the no-comments record with 0 problems; with --no-tags it reports 'claims[3] commit 58bc6e8 is not in this repository'.
claims.remaining: Nothing stops the tag being deleted; H13 covers protecting refs.

next.item: Pin this commit in quality, finances and agent-ledger, add each one's .changes/exempt, and drop --observe from changes.yml and scripts/ci
next.why_now: This change is what those three were waiting for
next.impact: A code change in those repos can no longer merge without saying what it proved

next.item: Fix the four merged records that are VERIFIED with no commit in quality and finances
next.why_now: Under enforcement, the next pull request that edits one of them fails
next.impact: The records say which commit each check ran on, and editing them no longer blocks a pull request
